vehicleWarranty.heroTitle: Automating Vehicle Warranty Claims with AI Document Intelligence
vehicleWarranty.heroSubtitle: From 18% to 98% Decision Accuracy in 7 Days
vehicleWarranty.problemP1: A vehicle warranty claim lands on an adjuster's desk: five documents, three languages, a cost estimate with 30 line items, a policy with coverage tiers, mileage-dependent reimbursement rates and component exclusion lists.
vehicleWarranty.problemP2: Processing takes 15-30 minutes per claim. Multiply that by hundreds of claims per month.
vehicleWarranty.problemP3Start: 76% of denied claims fail for a single reason:
vehicleWarranty.problemP3Emphasis: the part is not covered by the policy
vehicleWarranty.problemP3End: - a deterministic lookup, not a judgment call.
vehicleWarranty.whyExistingFailIntro: Most document processing tools extract text from PDFs - that gets you 10% of the way. The real challenge is
vehicleWarranty.whyExistingFailIntroEnd: : a cost estimate means nothing without the policy, a mileage reading means nothing without the coverage cap.

genericOcr.title: Generic OCR pipelines lack domain depth
genericOcr.desc: Swiss repair invoices contain line items in German with part numbers, labor codes, carry-forward subtotals across pages. Standard OCR extracts text but not structured data with coverage implications.

singleModel.title: Single-model approaches plateau early
singleModel.desc: Sending an entire claim to an LLM produces inconsistent results - hallucinated part names, invented coverage rules, unreliable financial calculations. Baseline LLM-only accuracy: 18%.

ruleBased.title: Rule-based systems cannot scale to vocabulary
ruleBased.desc: Thousands of part names across multiple languages. A "Wasserpumpe" in German is a "pompe à eau" in French. Pure keyword matching breaks on the first synonym it has not seen.

vehicleWarranty.hybridSolutionEnd: : deterministic rules where they work, keyword matching for known vocabulary and LLM reasoning as a calibrated fallback - each layer with explicit confidence scoring and provenance tracking.
vehicleWarranty.architectureIntro: An end-to-end claims processing pipeline moves raw documents through five stages, each with quality gates and audit logging.

multiTier.heading: Coverage Analysis: Multi-Tier Matching
multiTier.intro: Each line item goes through a multi-tier matching pipeline, prioritizing deterministic approaches before falling back to AI:

deterministic.name: Deterministic Rules
deterministic.desc: Exact matches for known items, exclusions, and consumables. Zero ambiguity, instant resolution.

keyword.name: Keyword Matching
keyword.desc: Maps multilingual repair terms to component categories with synonym normalization.

aiFallback.name: AI Fallback
aiFallback.desc: LLM with structured prompts for genuinely ambiguous items that require contextual reasoning.

expandable.stage1Desc: Pluggable ingestion layer supporting multiple OCR providers for production workloads. Each page extracted independently with position tracking for full provenance.
expandable.stage2Desc: AI-powered router classifies documents by type with language-specific cues across German, French, and Italian. Near-100% classification accuracy.
expandable.stage3Desc: Domain-specific extractors handle comprehensive field sets for warranty policies. Cost estimate extractors handle multi-page documents with carry-forward subtotals and total validation. Every field carries a confidence score, provenance and quality gate verdict.
expandable.screeningIntro: The screening pipeline runs multiple deterministic checks covering policy validity, coverage eligibility, and compliance requirements. Each check produces one of three verdicts:
expandable.softCheckDesc: Flags for attention but doesn't block
expandable.screeningNote: Checks cover areas like policy status, coverage dates, mileage limits, component eligibility, and exclusion patterns.
expandable.payoutIntro: The payout calculation follows insurer-specific business rules, typically including:

payoutItems.applyCaps: Applying coverage caps and reimbursement rates

expandable.payoutNote: Each insurer has specific rules for deductibles, reimbursement tiers, and parts/labor splits that must be matched exactly.

day1_3.label: Days 1-3
day1_3.title: Baseline and Architecture
day1_3.desc: The initial LLM-only approach produced plausible-sounding but unreliable results: hallucinated part names, invented coverage rules, inconsistent calculations.
day1_3.insightText: LLMs are good at language understanding but bad at deterministic business rules. The architecture had to separate judgment from precision.

day3_5.label: Days 3-5
day3_5.title: Screening + Coverage Pipeline
day3_5.desc: The deterministic screening pipeline and multi-tier coverage matching drove the biggest single improvement. Rule-based checks alone caught most denials correctly.

day5_8.label: Days 5-8
day5_8.title: Iteration and Refinement
day5_8.desc: 60+ evaluation iterations solving increasingly subtle problems: substring matching bugs, labor demotion logic, and part-number normalization across OCR outputs.

holdout.label: Holdout Test
holdout.title: Unseen Data Validation
holdout.desc: 30 previously unseen claims revealed failure modes the development set did not cover: causal exclusion clauses, missing document scenarios and sub-component interpretation gaps.
holdout.honest: The holdout gap (98% vs 77%) is the honest measure of generalization.

iterationDetails.title: Detailed iteration fixes (88% to 98%)
iterationDetails.substringBugDesc: An EGR valve synonym ("abgasrueckfuehrung") contained the substring "asr" (anti-slip regulation). The system declared the EGR valve covered under brakes. Fix: symmetric guard requiring exact match when either term is 3 characters or fewer.
iterationDetails.laborDemotionDesc: When a part was covered, the associated installation labor should also be covered. Fix: labor promotion logic that inherits coverage from the parent repair.
iterationDetails.partNumberDesc: A Mercedes part number was not matched due to spacing differences in OCR extraction. Fix: normalize all part numbers by stripping spaces and special characters before lookup.

causal.title: Causal exclusion clauses
causal.desc: A turbocharger is covered, but if the turbo failed because the engine (not covered) failed first, the policy denies coverage. The system does not reason about failure chains.

missingDocs.title: Missing documents
missingDocs.desc: One claim was denied because the policy premium was not paid. This information lives in the insurer's internal system, not in any processable document.

subComponent.title: Sub-component interpretation gaps
subComponent.desc: A DPF sensor is functionally part of the exhaust system. The policy covers exhausts but only lists specific sub-components. The adjuster approved by interpreting the sensor as an exhaust sub-component.

excludedDominance.title: Excluded-component dominance
excludedDominance.desc: A claim for a hose repair (excluded) was approved because a minor bolt (CHF 3.70, covered) was also on the invoice.

multiLang.title: Multi-Language Processing
multiLang.desc: Language-aware classification and extraction across German, French and Italian. Comparable approval rates with no measurable language bias.

auditability.title: Auditability and Compliance
auditability.desc: Full provenance chain: every extracted field links to its source document and page. Every coverage decision includes match method, confidence score and explanation.

payoutPrecision.title: Payout Formula Precision
payoutPrecision.desc: Order-of-operations errors in financial calculations can cause significant overpayment. Finding them requires walking through calculations claim by claim with adjusters.

costControl.title: Cost Control
costControl.desc: Deterministic rules and keyword matching handle the majority of items with zero LLM cost. Token usage monitoring with configurable thresholds prevents runaway costs.

orderOfOps.title: Order-of-operations lesson
orderOfOps.intro: When applying degraded reimbursement rates, the order of operations matters:
orderOfOps.wrongDesc: Apply rate after VAT and deductible calculations
orderOfOps.correctDesc: Apply rate to covered amount first, then add VAT and subtract deductible
orderOfOps.note: A single operation-order error can cause significant overpayment. Finding these bugs requires walking through calculations with adjusters.

lesson1.title: Deterministic checks beat LLM judgment for structured rules.
lesson1.desc: 76% of claim denials are "part not covered" - a lookup, not a judgment call. The screening pipeline handles these with 100% confidence and zero LLM cost.

lesson2.title: The accuracy curve has diminishing returns.
lesson2.desc: 18% to 76% took 3 days. 76% to 98% took 4 more days. The holdout gap (98% vs 77%) confirmed that real-world generalization requires significantly more data.

lesson3.title: The payout formula is harder than the AI.
lesson3.desc: Getting the financial calculation to match the insurer's exact formula requires sitting with an adjuster and walking through calculations by hand. No amount of prompt engineering solves a business logic bug.

lesson4.title: Provenance tracking is non-negotiable.
lesson4.desc: In a regulated industry, every extracted value and coverage decision must trace back to a source document. Fundamental to trust and compliance.

nextSteps.heading: Next Steps Taken
nextSteps.step2: Integrated with insurer's policy management API for real-time status checks
nextSteps.step3: Implemented causal exclusion reasoning for cascading-damage denials
nextSteps.step4: Deployed production triage: auto-reject high-confidence denials, auto-approve simple approvals, route edge cases for human review
nextSteps.conclusion: The goal is not to replace adjusters but to give them back their time on the 76% of denials that are straightforward lookups, so they can focus their expertise on the 24% that actually require judgment.
